name: Cathedral Basilica of the Sacred Heart
history: Construction began in 1899 and took 55 years; the cathedral was consecrated on 19 October 1954. It was first planned in an English-Irish Gothic style and changed to French Gothic. It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Newark and the fifth-largest cathedral in North America.
arch: Often called the most exact example of French Gothic architecture in the Western Hemisphere. It is roughly the size of Westminster Abbey, with towers taller than those of Notre-Dame in Paris.
features: The 36-foot rose window over the main entrance is the largest in the Catholic Church in the Western Hemisphere.
It has the largest organ Schantz ever built, the biggest church organ in New Jersey.

look.d: 36 feet across: the largest Catholic rose window in the Western Hemisphere.
These towers rise higher than those of Notre-Dame in Paris.

fun: John Paul II visited in 1995 and named it a basilica the same year.
journal: Fifty-five years of stone, and it really does feel like France on Branch Brook Park.
